results: 1. Detailed bedside neurological and cranial-nerve examination, including voluntary and emotional facial movements, forehead wrinkling, eye closure, cheek puffing, smiling, and speech
cranial nerve examination: bilateral post-paralytic facial synkinesis; narrowed left palpebral fissure
deep tendon reflexes and plantar responses: normal
synkinesis assessment (eye closure with platysma/frontalis): co-contraction of eye closure with the left platysma and left frontalis; right lower-lip curling on speech and mastication
palpebral fissure width both sides: narrowed LEFT palpebral fissure from established synkinesis
gait, ability to run, and limb sensation: normal
2. Review of prior medical records, neurological examinations, and photographs or videos documenting the earlier episode

clinical course: left facial palsy treated with acyclovir 400 mg five times daily for 10 days and prednisone 50 mg for five days with taper; right palsy at age 64 with retroauricular pain, hyperacusis and dysgeusia; right synkinesis appeared five months later
3. MRI of the brain with diffusion-weighted imaging
4. MRI of the brain and skull base with and without gadolinium
MRI brain and internal auditory canal with contrast: no tumour, no perineural enhancement, no central lesion
5. Electromyography and nerve-conduction studies of the facial nerves
electroneuronography / facial EMG: chronic reinnervation with synkinetic co-activation; no active denervation
7. Complete blood count, comprehensive metabolic panel, fasting lipid profile, and hemoglobin A1c
serum electrolytes, urea and creatinine: normal
full blood count and ESR/CRP: normal
dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Bilateral sequential recurrent idiopathic facial nerve palsy (recurrent Bell’s palsy) with chronic post-paralytic facial synkinesis

ALTERNATIVE 1: Melkersson–Rosenthal syndrome

ALTERNATIVE 2: Neurosarcoidosis

ALTERNATIVE 3: Lyme neuroborreliosis
